Alex/Hannah — initial materials attached. High level notes below and a few open questions we should confirm on the call.

Summary of the attached diagram (vpc-control-data-impedance-diagram.pdf):
- Control plane: colocated in a management subnet with a tightly restricted NAT egress path to a monitored egress proxy in the customer VPC. All control-plane outbound requests are forced through the proxy; no direct internet egress from management instances.
- Data plane: tenant workloads run in isolated tenant subnets with explicit ACLs and GW routes. Cross-tenant traffic only via the Redwood data-proxy where we enforce tenancy labels and mTLS.
- Inter-region failover: KV cache synchronization uses an encrypted replication channel between regional data planes; control-plane failover is orchestrated via a multi-zone HA controller with staged promotion and traffic drain.

Runbook highlights (runbook-draft.md):
- Pre-cutover checks: control-plane health probes, egress proxy config validation, acceptance test suite (simple inference and auth).
- Canary steps: deploy subset tenants (5%), monitor tail-latency and token-error rates, validate KVC replication lag < 50ms, then ramp.
- Rollback: immediate control-plane rollback policy + data-plane session drain window.

Open questions for Skybridge:
1) Do you require control-plane telemetry to be sent to your SIEM (we can forward via a secure collector)?
2) Any retention constraints (beyond 90 days) for audit logs we should bake into the evidence pack?

Drive link with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_private_vpc_review

Attachments: vpc-control-data-impedance-diagram.pdf, runbook-draft.md

—Mina

Thanks Mina — diagram and runbook look solid. A few inline redlines and suggestions below.

> Control plane: colocated in a management subnet with a tightly restricted NAT egress path to a monitored egress proxy in the customer VPC.
- Suggestion: call out the exact proxy endpoints and required allow-list ranges in an appendix (we'll put that in the final runbook). Also note TLS mutual-auth requirement for the proxy (customer cert + Redwood identity).

> Inter-region failover: KV cache synchronization uses an encrypted replication channel between regional data planes; control-plane failover is orchestrated via a multi-zone HA controller with staged promotion and traffic drain.
- Redline: add expected RPO/RTO numbers for both cache and control-plane failover (propose RPO=0s for cache using synchronous replication in the primary pair; RTO target 3 minutes for control-plane promotion).

Attached a short acceptance checklist CSV we use to capture evidence items during the procurement review. I'll also add a brief sample telemetry snippet (minimal PII) to the Drive.

On the call we should confirm: 1) allowlist / egress firewall specifics, 2) SIEM integration method, 3) retention SLA for audit logs.

Attachment: acceptance-criteria.csv

—Olga

Principal Deploy Engineer, Redwood Inference
